AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a fruit crop? (1 mark)
   A. Cabbage
   B. Spinach
   C. Sukuma wiki
   D. Guava

2. Which is a pest problem for ripe fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Stones
   B. Sand
   C. Fruit flies and birds
   D. Sun

3. What is a tree tomato? (1 mark)
   A. A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
   B. A vegetable that grows underground
   C. A cereal
   D. A climbing vine

4. What is a trellis? (1 mark)
   A. A type of fruit
   B. A support structure for climbing plants
   C. A tool for cutting
   D. A bag for seeds

5. What is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal found only in parks
   B. An animal kept and cared for by people
   C. An animal that lives freely in the forest
   D. An animal that cannot be tamed

6. Which nutrient in milk builds strong bones and teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Calcium
   C. Sugar
   D. Starch

7. What is the meat of sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Bacon
   B. Mutton
   C. Beef
   D. Pork

8. Which domestic animal is kept as a pet to guard the home? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Dog
   C. Cow
   D. Hen

9. Why is a meal of only chips not balanced? (1 mark)
   A. It lacks body-building and protective foods
   B. It has no energy
   C. It has too much protein
   D. It has too many vegetables

10. Which meal is missing protective foods? (1 mark)
   A. Sweet potato, egg and spinach
   B. Ugali, beans and cabbage
   C. Rice and fish only
   D. Githeri and avocado

11. Which of these fruits is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Orange
   B. Rice
   C. Chapati
   D. Butter

12. Which of these gives fibre? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetables and fruits
   B. Sweets
   C. Soft drinks
   D. Sugar

13. What should be done with a fire after cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it burning
   B. Cover it with paper
   C. Put it out or switch off the gas
   D. Add more wood

14. What should you hold hot pots with? (1 mark)
   A. A wet cloth
   B. Bare hands
   C. Paper
   D. A dry cloth or oven gloves

15. How much oil is used for shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. A whole bottle
   B. A full pot
   C. None
   D. A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan

16. Which food is cooked by deep frying and not shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. A fried egg
   B. Chapati in a pan
   C. Fish pieces in a pan
   D. Mandazi

17. About how long should you rub hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. About 1 second
   B. About 20 seconds
   C. About 5 minutes
   D. Not at all

18. What should you do after coughing into your hands? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Shake hands
   C. Wipe them on your clothes
   D. Wash your hands with soap and water

19. What can be used if there is no soap? (1 mark)
   A. Oil
   B. Sugar
   C. Clean ash and running water
   D. Mud

20. Why should you not dip hands into a drinking water container? (1 mark)
   A. Hands would get cold
   B. The water would evaporate
   C. The container would break
   D. Hands may put germs into the water

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how to prepare a planting hole for a fruit tree. (4 marks)

22. Describe how to boil potatoes. (4 marks)

23. List four safety rules when cooking. (4 marks)

24. Explain how animals help crops grow. (3 marks)

25. Explain the difference between variety and proportion in a meal. (3 marks)

26. Describe how to boil eggs. (4 marks)

27. How do fruits help our health? (3 marks)

28. Name three PPE items and what each protects. (3 marks)

29. Why should fruit be washed before it is eaten? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Guava
   Guava is a fruit.

2. C — Fruit flies and birds
   Ripe fruit attracts flies and birds.

3. A — A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
   Tree tomato is a woody tree fruit.

4. B — A support structure for climbing plants
   A trellis is posts and wires to hold climbers.

5. B — An animal kept and cared for by people
   Domestic animals depend on people for food, water and shelter.

6. B — Calcium
   Milk has calcium and protein.

7. B — Mutton
   Mutton is sheep meat.

8. B — Dog
   Dogs guard homes.

9. A — It lacks body-building and protective foods
   Chips give mainly energy.

10. C — Rice and fish only
   Rice and fish have energy and protein but no vegetables or fruits.

11. A — Orange
   Fruits are protective foods.

12. A — Vegetables and fruits
   Fibre helps digestion.

13. C — Put it out or switch off the gas
   This prevents accidents and saves fuel.

14. D — A dry cloth or oven gloves
   Wet cloth lets heat through.

15. D — A small amount that covers the bottom of the pan
   Shallow frying uses a thin layer.

16. D — Mandazi
   Mandazi float in deep oil.

17. B — About 20 seconds
   This is long enough to clean properly.

18. D — Wash your hands with soap and water
   Germs from coughs stay on hands.

19. C — Clean ash and running water
   Ash helps to remove dirt when soap is not available.

20. D — Hands may put germs into the water
   Use a clean cup or tap.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a sunny site; dig a hole about half a metre wide and deep; put topsoil aside; mix topsoil with compost; put some mixture back in the hole.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash, peel and cut into equal pieces; put in a pot with water and salt; cover and boil for about 15 to 20 minutes until soft; drain the water carefully.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cook with an adult; turn handles inward; use a dry cloth for hot pots; open lids away from the face; keep water away from hot oil (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Their dung is used as manure, which feeds the soil, and oxen can be used to plough. Crops then grow well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for manure, 1 for ploughing, 1 for better crops.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Variety is eating many kinds of food; proportion is eating the right amount of each kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for variety, 1 mark for proportion, 1 mark for an example.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put eggs in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, boil gently for about 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins that fight illness, fibre that helps digestion and water that keeps the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remove dirt and germs so it is safe to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for germs or safety.
